sources.title: Machine learning and the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns

hypothesis: Cross-sectional momentum in liquid cryptocurrencies is concentrated in bullish market regimes; restricting a long-only winner portfolio to BTC-positive regimes should retain the tradable long-leg anomaly while avoiding weak/choppy periods and short-side frictions.
universe: Frozen ex-ante Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals listed by 2021-12-31, including later-delisted contracts where data exist. Each Monday retain top 30 by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume.
asset_signal: 30-day close-to-close momentum using only completed prior days.
regime: BTCUSDT trailing R-day close return through Sunday. Trade only if positive.
portfolio: When regime is ON, equal-weight long top momentum quintile at 1.0 gross; otherwise cash. No short leg.
execution: Rebalance Monday 00:00 UTC open using data through Sunday; hold to next Monday open. Closing to cash on OFF weeks incurs turnover costs.
development_gate: Canonical active-week rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, at least 2/3 regime lookbacks positive, and at least 20 active development weeks.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; positive at 2x costs; at least 2/3 regime variants positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; at least 20 active OOS weeks; excluding BTC/ETH remains positive; excluding strongest contributor remains positive; DSR reported.
notes: This is not a post-hoc retune of the prior unconditional momentum candidate. The regime restriction and long-only construction are directly motivated by published evidence that crypto momentum is regime-dependent and that economically viable predictability is concentrated in tradable long legs.
